prompt:
Our trading analytics platform needs its batch processing pipeline properly scheduled. We have four jobs in /workspace/scripts/ that need to run on strict schedules, and an archival service that needs a modern, robust scheduling setup.

Here are the business requirements:
1. The market data ingestion job (`ingest.sh`) must run every 15 minutes, but ONLY during market hours — Monday through Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM. It absolutely cannot overlap itself (if one run is still going when the next is due, skip the new run).
2. The daily trading report (`daily_report.sh`) must run at 6:30 AM on weekdays only.
3. The quarterly data cleanup (`quarterly_cleanup.sh`) must run at the stroke of midnight on the 1st of January, April, July, and October.
4. The preflight check script (`preflight.sh`) must run automatically every time the server boots up.
5. All of the above (items 1-4) should be configured together in a single crontab file named `pipeline.crontab`. This system operates globally across timezones and we've been burned by daylight saving time before — all schedules must be completely immune to DST clock changes.
6. The archive job (`archive.sh`) needs a more modern, resilient scheduling setup using two separate files: `archive.service` and `archive.timer`. It should run daily at 3:00 AM, survive server reboots (catching up on any missed runs), and include a small random delay (up to 5 minutes) to avoid thundering-herd problems.
7. Finally, the existing `scripts/job_wrapper.sh` script is a placeholder stub. Replace it with a real implementation that wraps any command with proper logging (including start time, end time, and elapsed duration), captures the exit code, and logs both success and failure outcomes.

Please set everything up in the /workspace directory.
